## Idea
A pure four-word 32-bit pseudorandom state. Draws return both the value and successor state; split uses a jump-separated stream.

## Complexity
next/state/seed have fixed-width bounded cost. Rejection sampling for bounded draws has variable work. jump/split use a fixed polynomial. State O(1).

## Use when
Reproducible simulation draws and explicit state threading are required.

## Avoid when
Cryptographic unpredictability or a proof of independent arbitrary seeds is required.

## Pitfalls
Never reuse the old state for a new draw. All-zero state is refused. nextFloat is Portable; integer-state/draw operations are LockstepExact. Jump-separated streams are not a cryptographic independence guarantee.

## F# usage
Package: FS.GG.Algorithms; cited source API (resolve your actual package pin).
`FS.GG.Algorithms.Random.Xoshiro128.nextBelow: int -> Xoshiro128 -> struct (int * Xoshiro128)`

```fsharp
open FS.GG.Algorithms.Random
let stream = Xoshiro128.seed 73
let struct (die, nextState) = Xoshiro128.nextBelow 6 stream
```

These are GitHub-hosted runner-class comparisons, not quiet-host absolute performance; this later source revision is not itself remeasured.
